reach.rationale: Every API the code itself calls is long-stable; the only 'new' element is the toolchain (TS 7 native, Vite 8/Rolldown), which is the current stable release, so reach is nearly minimal — docked one point only because TS 7.0/Vite 8 are months, not years, old and TS 7.0 has known ecosystem gaps.

app/ — no vite.config.* exists at all, so zero bundler flags to contain

containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain, and what platform access exists is already funneled through small wrapper modules (api.ts, dom.ts), so any future API change would be a one-file edit.

justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and the very-new-but-stable toolchain is used exactly within its documented, safe envelope (CLI typecheck, zero-config Vite), so every choice buys speed or simplicity without novelty risk.

findings.issue: typescript 7.0.2 is the .0 minor line of the brand-new native compiler (GA 2026-07-08) and lacks the programmatic API until 7.1; ecosystem integrations (frameworks, eslint) still catching up.
findings.suggestion: Fine as used here (CLI-only typecheck), but pin with a lockfile (already present) and be ready to hold at 7.0.x if tooling regressions appear.

summary: The app is maximally conservative on the experimentalness axis: zero experimental/preview flags, no Vite config, and every runtime API it touches (fetch, replaceChildren, AbortSignal.timeout, history, normalize) has been Baseline-stable for years. The only recency is the toolchain — TypeScript 7 (native, GA 2026-07-08) and Vite 8 with Rolldown (GA 2026-03-12) — both verified as the frameworks' current stable releases and used only through their safest, most standard entry points. There is essentially no breakage surface from experimental APIs.
